items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
               <jats:p>Let <jats:italic>m</jats:italic> be a natural number, and let <jats:inline-formula id="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9999_w2aab3b8e3082b1b7b1aab1c13b1b3Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mi>𝒬</m:mi>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" content-type="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9999" xlink:href="graphic/j_forum-2014-0137_eq_mi695.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>${\mathscr{Q}}$</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula> be a set containing at least <jats:inline-formula id="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9998_w2aab3b8e3082b1b7b1aab1c13b1b5Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mrow>
                              <m:mi>exp</m:mi>
                              <m:mo>⁡</m:mo>
                              <m:mrow>
                                 <m:mo>(</m:mo>
                                 <m:mrow>
                                    <m:mi>C</m:mi>
                                    <m:mo>⁢</m:mo>
                                    <m:mi>m</m:mi>
                                 </m:mrow>
                                 <m:mo>)</m:mo>
                              </m:mrow>
                           </m:mrow>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" content-type="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9998" xlink:href="graphic/j_forum-2014-0137_eq_mi651.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>${\exp(Cm)}$</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula> primes. We show that one can find infinitely many strings of <jats:italic>m</jats:italic> consecutive primes each of which has some <jats:inline-formula id="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9997_w2aab3b8e3082b1b7b1aab1c13b1b9Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mrow>
                              <m:mi>q</m:mi>
                              <m:mo>∈</m:mo>
                              <m:mi>𝒬</m:mi>
                           </m:mrow>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" content-type="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9997" xlink:href="graphic/j_forum-2014-0137_eq_mi800.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>${q\in\mathscr{Q}}$</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula> as a primitive root, all lying in an interval of length <jats:inline-formula id="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9996_w2aab3b8e3082b1b7b1aab1c13b1c11Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mrow>
                              <m:msub>
                                 <m:mi>O</m:mi>
                                 <m:mi>𝒬</m:mi>
                              </m:msub>
                              <m:mo>⁢</m:mo>
                              <m:mrow>
                                 <m:mo>(</m:mo>
                                 <m:mrow>
                                    <m:mi>exp</m:mi>
                                    <m:mo>⁡</m:mo>
                                    <m:mrow>
                                       <m:mo>(</m:mo>
                                       <m:mrow>
                                          <m:msup>
                                             <m:mi>C</m:mi>
                                             <m:mo>′</m:mo>
                                          </m:msup>
                                          <m:mo>⁢</m:mo>
                                          <m:mi>m</m:mi>
                                       </m:mrow>
                                       <m:mo>)</m:mo>
                                    </m:mrow>
                                 </m:mrow>
                                 <m:mo>)</m:mo>
                              </m:mrow>
                           </m:mrow>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" content-type="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9996" xlink:href="graphic/j_forum-2014-0137_eq_mi602.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>${O_{\mathscr{Q}}(\exp(C^{\prime}m))}$</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula>. This is a bounded gaps variant of a theorem of Gupta and Ram Murty. We also prove a result on an elliptic analogue of Artin’s conjecture. Let <jats:inline-formula id="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9995_w2aab3b8e3082b1b7b1aab1c13b1c13Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mrow>
                              <m:mi>E</m:mi>
                              <m:mo>/</m:mo>
                              <m:mi>ℚ</m:mi>
                           </m:mrow>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" content-type="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9995" xlink:href="graphic/j_forum-2014-0137_eq_mi555.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>${E/\mathbb{Q}}$</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula> be an elliptic curve with an irrational 2-torsion point. Assume GRH. Then for every <jats:italic>m</jats:italic>, there are infinitely many strings of <jats:italic>m</jats:italic> consecutive primes <jats:italic>p</jats:italic> for which <jats:inline-formula id="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9994_w2aab3b8e3082b1b7b1aab1c13b1c21Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mrow>
                              <m:mi>E</m:mi>
                              <m:mo>⁢</m:mo>
                              <m:mrow>
                                 <m:mo>(</m:mo>
                                 <m:msub>
                                    <m:mi>𝔽</m:mi>
                                    <m:mi>p</m:mi>
                                 </m:msub>
                                 <m:mo>)</m:mo>
                              </m:mrow>
                           </m:mrow>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" content-type="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9994" xlink:href="graphic/j_forum-2014-0137_eq_mi553.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>${E(\mathbb{F}_{p})}$</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula> is cyclic, all lying an interval of length <jats:inline-formula id="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9993_w2aab3b8e3082b1b7b1aab1c13b1c23Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:mrow>
                              <m:msub>
                                 <m:mi>O</m:mi>
                                 <m:mi>E</m:mi>
                              </m:msub>
                              <m:mo>⁢</m:mo>
                              <m:mrow>
                                 <m:mo>(</m:mo>
                                 <m:mrow>
                                    <m:mi>exp</m:mi>
                                    <m:mo>⁡</m:mo>
                                    <m:mrow>
                                       <m:mo>(</m:mo>
                                       <m:mrow>
                                          <m:msup>
                                             <m:mi>C</m:mi>
                                             <m:mi>′′</m:mi>
                                          </m:msup>
                                          <m:mo>⁢</m:mo>
                                          <m:mi>m</m:mi>
                                       </m:mrow>
                                       <m:mo>)</m:mo>
                                    </m:mrow>
                                 </m:mrow>
                                 <m:mo>)</m:mo>
                              </m:mrow>
                           </m:mrow>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" content-type="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9993" xlink:href="graphic/j_forum-2014-0137_eq_mi598.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>${O_{E}(\exp(C^{\prime\prime}m))}$</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula>. If <jats:italic>E</jats:italic> has CM, then the GRH assumption can be removed. Here <jats:italic>C</jats:italic>, <jats:inline-formula id="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9992_w2aab3b8e3082b1b7b1aab1c13b1c29Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:msup>
                              <m:mi>C</m:mi>
                              <m:mo>′</m:mo>
                           </m:msup>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" content-type="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9992" xlink:href="graphic/j_forum-2014-0137_eq_mi543.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>${C^{\prime}}$</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula>, and <jats:inline-formula id="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9991_w2aab3b8e3082b1b7b1aab1c13b1c31Aa">
                     <jats:alternatives>
                        <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                           <m:msup>
                              <m:mi>C</m:mi>
                              <m:mi>′′</m:mi>
                           </m:msup>
                        </m:math>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" content-type="j_forum-2014-0137_eq_9991" xlink:href="graphic/j_forum-2014-0137_eq_mi541.png"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>${C^{\prime\prime}}$</jats:tex-math>
                     </jats:alternatives>
                  </jats:inline-formula> are absolute constants.</jats:p>
title: Bounded gaps between primes with a given primitive root, II
